private_notes.private_reasoning: The class has strong merits but meaningful certification and trial risk, so I should open above the expected litigation value while emphasizing reliable, meaningful relief. Automatic distribution is important because Brightline can identify every member. I will avoid a clear-sailing commitment and ensure any court-rejected fee benefits the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

Open with a strong class-centered anchor. The identified class can receive money automatically, so insist on automatic distribution and avoid a claims process. Fees do not affect the firm's compensation; request a substantial but separate fee while protecting the class if the court awards less than requested. Do not accept any term sheet yet.

Neither opening proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Make a credible but lower counteroffer that preserves automatic distribution, avoids a fee guarantee, and directs any court-declined fees to the class. Keep room to negotiate in later rounds.
